title: Bittensor Daily News: November 16, 2026
summary: Ms. Computer announces hosting and agent sandboxes on SN24. Engy reports 3.11 trillion inference tokens over 30 closed UTC days, while Hippius releases a mobile sharing update.

updates.headline: SN24 ms.computer announces hosting and AI-agent sandboxes
updates.summary:
Ms. Computer announced its SN24 launch on November 15 at 2:20 PM Eastern, presenting HOST for free website or app hosting and RUN for an AI agent in its own sandbox. CONNECT, its inference-network offering, is explicitly marked coming soon. The announcement also invites users to a waitlist, so the launch should not be read as proof of unrestricted access to every service.

The linked public miner repository describes software that runs customer workloads in an isolated sandbox on a miner’s host. Its documentation says validators check advertised resources and service delivery, with roughly four hours of qualification after enablement before a miner can earn. The software is proprietary and source-available, with permission to run it unmodified for SN24 mining.

This moves the story beyond the earlier rename and owner-address coverage to an announced service offering. We verified the team’s announcement and published documentation; we did not deploy a customer workload or verify paid demand.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: an announced hosting and agent-compute offering materially changes what SN24 provides, exceeding routine maintenance at three. Five is not established by the currently documented access and deployment scope.

updates.headline: SN53 Engy reports 3.11 trillion inference tokens over 30 days
updates.summary:
Engy’s public dashboard reported 3,105,679,412,402 prompt and completion tokens across the last 30 closed UTC days, October 17 through November 15. The dashboard snapshot was updated at 14:00 UTC on November 16. It describes the figures as buyer traffic across live catalog models, excluding Engy’s own probes.

The period averaged about 103.52 billion tokens a day and peaked at 190.72 billion on November 13. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash accounted for about 83.5% of the total, showing that most throughput came from one model rather than an even spread across the nine listed models.

These are operator-reported usage figures, not independently audited revenue or profit. Token throughput alone does not establish customer counts, margins or a fair token valuation. We have not carried forward the secondary article’s Venice valuation comparison because a comparable, independently checked measurement basis was not established in this review.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a quantified multi-trillion-token usage milestone is substantial operational evidence for the subnet, beyond a routine model listing at three. Five is not supported by the reported scope alone or by an unverified valuation comparison.

updates.headline: SN75 Hippius adds mobile uploads and sharing in Drive 1.3.0
updates.summary:
Hippius announced Drive 1.3.0 on November 16, saying the update is live on iOS and Android. It adds uploads through other apps’ share buttons, drive sharing and invitations from a phone, and links from WhatsApp, Messages or email that open directly in the Hippius app.

The change makes the existing storage product easier to use in everyday mobile workflows. This is an update to the app, not a newly demonstrated storage network or adoption milestone. The release details are attributed to the team; device installation and regional store availability were not independently tested.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: useful mobile upload and sharing capabilities improve an existing product. Two understates the workflow change; four would overstate this bounded app update.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: useful mobile upload and sharing capabilities improve an existing product. Two understates the workflow change; four would overstate this bounded app update.
